Subject: Question: cookie mapping & DPA — Handshake / Redwood

Hi Hannah,

Hope you’re well. I’m Elena (Privacy Lead) at Handshake AI — we’re kicking off a security/privacy review ahead of a potential pilot and had a few clarifying questions about how Redwood handles tracking/cookies and telemetry related to the console and hosted service. Specifically: 

- Does Redwood set any marketing/analytics cookies or persistent identifiers when a customer uses the Redwood Console (app.redwood.ai) or embeds any of your customer-facing SDKs? If so, which categories (necessary, analytics, marketing)?
- Are console/telemetry events tied to IP addresses or other directly identifying attributes? If so, how long are they retained and are they pseudonymized?
- For hosted deployments, which subprocessors process telemetry/analytics (e.g., Amplitude/Mixpanel, Datadog)? Can you provide a current subprocessors list and note which are outside the EU?
- Do you rely on SCCs / EU standard contractual clauses for transfers, or do customers sign a specific DPA annex covering transfers to the US?

If helpful, attaching a short table of our requirements; otherwise a pointer to your DPA + subprocessors CSV is great. We’re aiming to complete vendor selection by mid-July.

Thanks — appreciate the quick help.

Best,
Elena Soto

Short answers up front:
- Transfers: For hosted accounts we rely on our DPA which includes standard contractual clauses (SCCs) for data transfers from the EEA to the U.S. Customers can also request a DPA annex for additional contractual terms; we’ve included a DPA excerpt in the attachment.
- Subprocessors: The attached CSV lists subprocessors in use for the service plane, telemetry, observability, and CDN. Some vendors operate US-hosted backends (marked in the CSV).
- SOC2 and audits: We make our SOC 2 Type II report available under NDA. If you need that to proceed we can start the NDA process and share the report.

Notes / caveats:
- The DPA covers processing of customer data. Telemetry described below is operational telemetry (console usage, performance metrics) and is scoped in our processing categories. If Handshake plans to send end-user personal data into Redwood hosted models, please flag that — it has additional requirements.

Hi Elena — technical follow-up from infra/telemetry. Quick bullets to address your points: 

- IPs: Application-level logs temporarily contain client IPs for troubleshooting and routing; for analytics/event streams we pseudonymize IPs by truncation and do not retain full source IP in Amplitude/analytics exports. Retention windows are configurable but default is 90 days for product telemetry and 13 months for operational logs (SOC/audit storage may be longer).
- Cookies: The Redwood Console uses first-party session cookies for auth and UX (session cookie, 3rd-party none by default). We do not set marketing pixels or cross-site tracking cookies from the console by default. Customers can add their own analytics integrations if they choose (that would be controlled by the customer and documented in their implementation guide).
- Vendors / subprocessors: The current subprocessors CSV (attached by Neha) lists: AWS (compute/S3), Google Cloud (some regions), Cloudflare/Fastly (edge), Datadog (observability), Sentry (error capture), Amplitude (product analytics), Segment (optional integration routing), SendGrid (system emails). Of these, Amplitude and Datadog receive event-level telemetry (Amplitude = product analytics; Datadog = metrics/traces). Payloads do not include customer PII by default — we strip obvious identifiers; if a customer sends PII into the service (e.g., model inputs that contain PII) that data will be present in telemetry unless the customer requests masking.
- EU-only tenancy: For hosted accounts we can pin data residency to an EU region for primary data at rest (EU region option available on contracts/ordering). Note that some global subprocessors (monitoring, CDN) may have control-plane components in other regions; that is reflected in the subprocessors CSV.
